 6 weather alerts in effect South Dakota workers to see minimum wage increase Jan. 1 
 The minimum wage for non-tipped employees will increase to $12.30 per hour, while the tipped minimum wage will rise to $6.15. 
 Download the KOTA News App. By Tamara Chibe Published : Nov. 17, 2026 at 2:52 PM CST | Updated : 18 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - South Dakota’s minimum wage is set to increase by 45 cents per hour beginning Jan. 1, 2027, giving workers earning the state minimum a higher hourly rate in the new year.
 The minimum wage for non-tipped employees will rise from $11.85 to $12.30 per hour, according to the South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation.
 The minimum wage for tipped employees will also increase, going from its current rate to $6.15 per hour. That rate is set at half the minimum wage for non-tipped workers.
 Employers must make sure employees’ combined wages and tips equal at least $12.30 per hour. If an employee’s tips do not bring their total earnings up to that amount, the employer must make up the difference.
 South Dakota adjusts its minimum wage annually based on changes in the cost of living. The calculation uses the Consumer Price Index published by the U.S. Department of Labor.
 The annual adjustments began after a state law took effect in 2016. The new rates apply to most employers in South Dakota, although state law includes some limited exceptions.
